geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a section-aware roof/upper mass to avoid a generic box and give the building a legible program section.
Use a folded section to create a calmer upper mass with a distinct public/private hierarchy.
Align the section to the long bar so the roof reads as a coherent response to the dominant gesture.
Promote the sectioned mass to root so the corrected dominant form becomes the compiled geometry.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic bar-like primary with a more articulated split mass so the body reads as one dominant gesture rather than two loosely colliding pieces.
Keep the split aligned to the long axis so the mass can preserve a single dominant rule.
Ensure the wings remain connected by a readable connector rather than becoming unrelated fragments.
Remove the overly sealed ground response and prepare space for a legible public seam at the access edge.
Lower the top heaviness so the section can support a calmer upper hierarchy over an active ground condition.
Deepen the carved void so it reads as usable public space rather than a shallow nibble.

rationale: The mass is understandable as a compact bar that has been split and bridged, but the four views do not fully agree on one dominant spatial idea. It reads as a clustered, stepped extrusion with some central opening, yet the void is not strong enough to become a legible public court or ground threshold. The blue frontage edge is not clearly answered by an open or carved access condition; the street response remains largely sealed. The silhouette is coherent enough to avoid total failure, but the section is still generic and more sculptural than programmatically useful for neighborhood living. The form remains inside the parcel and the repair does not appear over-clipped, so integrity is decent, but the dominant gesture is too weak and the public ground logic too underdeveloped for a hard pass.
